---
title: "Contrast environment screen"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: a first, cheap look at whether the subadult - adult contrast changes with weather
(option D, 2026-11-26; README "Downstream models"). It uses **no stage 1 output**: each
co-sampled survey event gives an empirical contrast with its sampling standard error, and a small
meta-regression across events and species asks whether those contrasts move with the weather at
the event. If it shows a signal, per-species moderation refits of stage 1 (option B) are the
formal follow-up.

What this can and cannot say:

- **seasonal-environmental, not weather**: raw 30-day temperature and 10-day precipitation are
  confounded with season (behavior, cohort growth, breeding). Only a climatology / anomaly split
  would support a weather interpretation.
- **co-sampled events only**: the only units that carry information about a stage x environment
  interaction. Species with few co-sampled events add little; *R. sierrae* has the most, but
  species-varying slopes keep it from setting the mean slope on its own.
- **between-site climate pending**: the site mean of swab-date weather is "climate at sampling
  time" (a summer-only site looks warm), so site climate waits for long-term normals (bioclim at
  site coordinates). Within-season and between-year terms are used here.

Run order: `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd` (model data), `01_contrast_tiers.Rmd` (species
table), then this script. Fits are small (hundreds of rows) and cached with `file =`.

# Setup
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, posterior, tidybayes)

screen_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "models", "environment_screen")
dir.create(screen_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")

# data file created by size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd
load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

# constants (min_swabs_unit, response_col), add_contrast_groups()
source(here("size_bd_contrast", "contrast_data_functions.R"))
# conv_check() (shared with the seasonal and contrast models)
source(here("size_bd_season", "season_check_functions.R"))

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

# included species (01_contrast_tiers.Rmd)
species_table = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_species.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
included = species_table %>% filter(include) %>% pull(taxon_capture)

# load events need a spread of log load in each stage: >= 2 positives per stage (one more than
# the load co-sampling rule, which needs only >= 1)
min_pos_screen = 2

```

# Events and climate
```{r}
contrast_data = brms_data %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% included) %>%
  add_contrast_groups() %>%
  mutate(temp = temp_c_30_day_mean,
         # precipitation on log2(1 + mm): a slope per doubling of 10-day rainfall
         precip = log2(1 + precip_mm_10_day_sum),
         log_load = if_else(.data[[response_col]] > 0, log(.data[[response_col]]), NA_real_))

# one row per event (all events, single-stage ones included: they define the site-year and site
# reference conditions). climate = mean over the event's swabs (79% of events are one day)
events = contrast_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, population, year, pop_year, pop_year_event) %>%
  summarise(temp = mean(temp), precip = mean(precip),
            n_ad = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult"),
            n_sub = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult"),
            pos_ad = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult" & !is.na(log_load)),
            pos_sub = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult" & !is.na(log_load)),
            mean_ll_ad = mean(log_load[life_stage_simple == "adult"], na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_ll_sub = mean(log_load[life_stage_simple == "subadult"], na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# climate split into three parts, within species:
#   *_within  event - its site-year mean      (within season)
#   *_year    site-year mean - its site mean  (between years at a site)
#   *_site    site mean - species mean        (between sites; NOT used: climate at sampling time)
# means are over events, so each event counts once whatever its swab count
events = events %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year) %>%
  mutate(temp_py = mean(temp), precip_py = mean(precip)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, population) %>%
  mutate(temp_pop = mean(temp_py), precip_pop = mean(precip_py)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  mutate(temp_within = temp - temp_py, precip_within = precip - precip_py,
         temp_year = temp_py - temp_pop, precip_year = precip_py - precip_pop,
         temp_site = temp_pop - mean(temp_pop), precip_site = precip_pop - mean(precip_pop)) %>%
  ungroup()

```

# Empirical contrasts
```{r}
# prevalence: empirical logit difference, subadult - adult (positive = subadults more often
# infected), with 0.5 added to each cell so 0/5 or 5/5 stay finite (Haldane correction).
# se = sqrt(sum of 1 / (cell + 0.5)) over the four cells
prev_events = events %>%
  filter(n_ad >= min_swabs_unit, n_sub >= min_swabs_unit) %>%
  mutate(contrast = log((pos_sub + 0.5) / (n_sub - pos_sub + 0.5)) -
           log((pos_ad + 0.5) / (n_ad - pos_ad + 0.5)),
         se = sqrt(1 / (pos_sub + 0.5) + 1 / (n_sub - pos_sub + 0.5) +
                     1 / (pos_ad + 0.5) + 1 / (n_ad - pos_ad + 0.5)))

# load: difference in mean log load among positives, subadult - adult. the se uses each species'
# pooled within-event sd of log load (2-3 positives alone give an unstable sd): residuals of log
# load around their event x stage mean, over all events with >= 2 positives in that stage
sd_log_load = contrast_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(log_load)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, pop_year_event, life_stage_simple) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  mutate(resid = log_load - mean(log_load)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(sd_ll = sqrt(sum(resid^2) / (n() - n_distinct(paste(pop_year_event, life_stage_simple)))),
            .groups = "drop")

load_events = events %>%
  filter(n_ad >= min_swabs_unit, n_sub >= min_swabs_unit,
         pos_ad >= min_pos_screen, pos_sub >= min_pos_screen) %>%
  left_join(sd_log_load, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(contrast = mean_ll_sub - mean_ll_ad,
         se = sd_ll * sqrt(1 / pos_sub + 1 / pos_ad))

# events per species: what each part rests on
full_join(count(prev_events, taxon_capture, name = "prevalence_events"),
          count(load_events, taxon_capture, name = "load_events"), by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  arrange(desc(prevalence_events))

# how much weather varies among the co-sampled events (sd of each part, per species): a slope
# needs spread. within-season spread is near 0 where co-sampled events are one per site-year
prev_events %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(c(temp_within, precip_within, temp_year, precip_year),
                            ~ round(sd(.x), 2)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

```

# Models
```{r}
# one meta-regression per part, with each event's sampling se known:
#   contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE)   y ~ N(mu, sqrt(sigma^2 + se^2)); sigma = event-to-event
#                                     variation beyond sampling noise
#   1 + temp_within + precip_within + temp_year + precip_year
#                                     mean contrast and its slopes (per degree C, per doubling of
#                                     10-day precipitation)
#   (1 + temp_within + precip_within | taxon_capture)
#                                     species mean contrasts and within-season slopes vary by
#                                     species (the population-level slope is then roughly a
#                                     species-weighted average). between-year slopes are shared,
#                                     to keep parameters few for sparse species
#   (1 | taxon_capture:population)    site-level contrasts
# no site-year level: co-sampled events are nearly one per site-year (e.g. r. sierrae 182 events,
# 161 site-years), so a site-year sd and sigma would not be separable (as R2 in stage 1).
# the null model drops the environment terms; comparing sigma and the site sd between the two
# says how much of the contrast's variation the environment explains.
env_formula = bf(contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + temp_within + precip_within + temp_year +
                   precip_year + (1 + temp_within + precip_within | taxon_capture) +
                   (1 | taxon_capture:population))
null_formula = bf(contrast | se(se, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + (1 | taxon_capture) +
                    (1 | taxon_capture:population))

# priors: weakly informative on the contrast scale (logit for prevalence, log load for load).
# slopes normal(0, 0.5): a 1 degree C or one doubling change moving the contrast by more than
# ~1 unit is implausible. sds as in stage 1: intercepts exponential(1), slopes exponential(2)
screen_priors = function(env = TRUE, intercept_sd = 2) {
  p = set_prior(paste0("normal(0, ", intercept_sd, ")"), class = "Intercept") +
    set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd") +
    set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma")
  if (env) {
    p = p + set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "b") +
      set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sd", group = "taxon_capture", coef = "temp_within") +
      set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sd", group = "taxon_capture", coef = "precip_within") +
      set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")
  }
  p
}

fit_screen = function(formula, data, prior, name) {
  brm(formula, data = data, family = gaussian(), prior = prior,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
      chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
      file = file.path(screen_dir, name), file_refit = "on_change")
}

screen_fits = list(
  prevalence_env  = fit_screen(env_formula,  prev_events, screen_priors(TRUE, 2),  "screen_prevalence_env"),
  prevalence_null = fit_screen(null_formula, prev_events, screen_priors(FALSE, 2), "screen_prevalence_null"),
  load_env        = fit_screen(env_formula,  load_events, screen_priors(TRUE, 3),  "screen_load_env"),
  load_null       = fit_screen(null_formula, load_events, screen_priors(FALSE, 3), "screen_load_null"))

# sampler checks (thresholds in conv_check)
map_dfr(screen_fits, conv_check, .id = "fit")

```

# Results
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

# population-level slopes: change in the contrast per degree C (temperature) or per doubling of
# 10-day precipitation. median, 50 / 95% intervals, pd
slope_draws = imap_dfr(screen_fits[c("prevalence_env", "load_env")], function(fit, name) {
  as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^b_(temp|precip)_", regex = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    pivot_longer(starts_with("b_"), names_to = "term", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(part = sub("_env$", "", name), term = sub("^b_", "", term))
})

(slope_summary = slope_draws %>%
  group_by(part, term) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value),
            lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
            lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))))

ggplot(slope_draws, aes(x = value, y = term)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), normalize = "panels") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "change in the subadult - adult contrast (per degree C / per doubling of precipitation)",
       y = NULL, subtitle = "population-level slopes; *_within = within season, *_year = between years at a site") +
  theme_classic()

# how much the environment explains: event-level sd (sigma) and site sd, null vs environment
# model. separate fits, so compare posterior summaries (not paired draws)
(variance_explained = imap_dfr(screen_fits, function(fit, name) {
  posterior_summary(fit, variable = c("sigma", "sd_taxon_capture:population__Intercept"),
                    probs = c(0.025, 0.975)) %>%
    as_tibble(rownames = "parameter") %>%
    mutate(fit = name)
}) %>%
  separate(fit, into = c("part", "model"), sep = "_") %>%
  select(part, model, parameter, Estimate, Q2.5, Q97.5) %>%
  arrange(part, parameter, model))

# out-of-sample comparison per part (small models: loo is cheap here)
map(c(prevalence = "prevalence", load = "load"), function(p) {
  loo_compare(loo(screen_fits[[paste0(p, "_env")]]), loo(screen_fits[[paste0(p, "_null")]]))
})

```

## Species slopes (within season)
```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10

# species-level within-season slopes (population slope + species deviation), for species with
# >= 10 co-sampled events in that part (fewer: the slope is mostly the population mean)
species_slopes = imap_dfr(list(prevalence = prev_events, load = load_events), function(ev, part) {
  fit = screen_fits[[paste0(part, "_env")]]
  keep = ev %>% count(taxon_capture) %>% filter(n >= 10) %>% pull(taxon_capture)
  fit %>%
    spread_draws(b_temp_within, b_precip_within,
                 r_taxon_capture[taxon_capture, term]) %>%
    filter(term %in% c("temp_within", "precip_within"), taxon_capture %in% keep) %>%
    mutate(value = if_else(term == "temp_within", b_temp_within, b_precip_within) + r_taxon_capture,
           part = part) %>%
    group_by(part, taxon_capture, term) %>%
    median_qi(value, .width = c(0.5, 0.95))
})

ggplot(species_slopes %>% filter(.width == 0.95),
       aes(x = value, xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper, y = taxon_capture)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(size = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(part ~ term, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "within-season slope (median, 95%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "species with >= 10 co-sampled events in that part") +
  theme_classic()

```

# Export
```{r}
write_csv(slope_summary, file.path(intermediates_dir, "04_environment_screen_slopes.csv"))
write_csv(variance_explained, file.path(intermediates_dir, "04_environment_screen_variance.csv"))

```
